title: Hugging Face and Cerebras Bring Gemma 4 to Real-Time Voice AI
hook: Multi-second delays are why voice assistants feel like phone menus. Running Gemma 4 on Cerebras hardware in a modular speech pipeline already powers 9,000+ Reachy Mini robots in production.
key_points: A speech-to-speech pipeline chains together: speech recognition (Nvidia Parakeet) -> Gemma 4 31B inference on Cerebras hardware -> text-to-speech (Alibaba Qwen3TTS) -> spoken response.
Each stage is modular and swappable, not a monolithic voice model.
The pitch is response time, not just accuracy: many voice systems hit frustrating multi-second delays at the P95, and Cerebras's inference speed targets exactly that bottleneck.
The pipeline already runs in production, powering over 9,000 Reachy Mini robots.
content_html: Voice assistants that pause for a beat before answering don't feel like a conversation — they feel like a phone menu. Hugging Face and Cerebras built a real-time voice pipeline around Gemma 4 specifically to close that gap.
extra_html:
The stack

The system chains four swappable, open components: speech recognition via Nvidia's Parakeet, language understanding and generation via Google DeepMind's Gemma 4 31B running on Cerebras hardware, and text-to-speech via Alibaba's Qwen3TTS. Cerebras's inference speed is the piece meant to solve the pipeline's biggest UX problem: many voice systems suffer multi-second delays at the P95 — long enough to break the feeling of a live exchange.

Why it matters

The announcement is explicit that for robots, voice assistants, and embodied AI, responsiveness isn't cosmetic — it's what makes an interaction feel alive rather than mechanical. It's not just a demo: the same pipeline already powers over 9,000 Reachy Mini robots in production, a reasonably concrete signal that fast, open-model voice pipelines are viable outside a lab setting.

related.title: Gemma 4: Google DeepMind's Open Multimodal Models
related.hook: An open-weight multimodal family (2.3B-31B) that now thinks before answering and, at 12B, skips separate vision/audio encoders entirely — still small enough for a 16GB laptop.
